{{Quote|The Darth title was more than just a symbol of power; it was a claim of supremacy. It was used by those Dark Lords who have sought to enforce their will on the other Masters. It was a challenge &mdash; a warning to bow down or be destroyed.|[[Sith Blademaster]], [[Kas'im]]|<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction" />}}
'''Darth''' was a title given to certain [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] which preceded either their chosen [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] name, or, in some cases, their birth name.

==Overview==
{{Quote|As lethal as you must be to become a lord, a Darth is the embodiment of death. Don't forget that.|Darth Baras to his back-cheeking apprentice|<ref name="SWTOR" />}}
[[File:Six_Sith_Lords.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Six famous Sith Lords bearing the Darth title, from left to right: [[Darth Andeddu]], [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan]], [[Darth Malak]], [[Darth Malgus]], [[Darth Ruin/Legends|Darth Ruin]], [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]].]]
Many [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] chose to add "Darth" to their name, so much so that the word is considered synonymous with the dark side of the Force in some circles. It was also taken to signify giving up one's old life. Such examples include Phanius becoming [[Darth Ruin/Legends|Darth Ruin]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] becoming Darth Vader. But the origins of the word are uncertain. It is often thought that "Darth" is merely a contraction of the title "[[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]]," but there are theories that suggest a deeper interpretation.<ref name="JvS" />

===Origins===
Some historians suggest that "Darth" is actually a corruption of the [[Rakata (language)|Rakata]] word ''[[Daritha]]'', meaning "emperor". Others note another Rakatan connection: the words for "triumph" or "conquest" in Rakatan is ''darr'', and the word for "death" is ''tah'', leading to the theory that "Darth" is derived from ''[[darr tah]]'' and therefore means "triumph over death" or "immortal". Given the Sith obsession with discovering the means to achieve immortality, this idea is not entirely without merit, at least on the surface. But others point out that the true meaning of ''darr tah'' is "conquest through death," meaning the conquest of one's enemies.<ref name="JvS" />

The "Darth" title is known to have existed before Revan and Malak's re-discovery of the Rakata and the Star Forge. Five years prior to their emergence as Sith Lords ([[3964 BBY]]), the Padawan [[Zayne Carrick]] called [[Jarael]] "Darth Sunshine."<ref name="KOTOR3">[[Knights of the Old Republic 3|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 3]]</ref> In addition, in [[3963 BBY]], [[Haazen]] claimed that if he were to take a name like the Sith of old, it would be "Darth Hayze."<ref name="KotOR 34">[[Knights of the Old Republic 34|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 34]]</ref> There is still the possibility that one of the Rakatan theories could be correct, since the ancient Sith homeworld of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] had once been [[Invasion of Korriban|invaded]] by the Rakata (circa [[27,700 BBY]]), which is one way either the ''Daritha'' or ''darr tah'' term could have entered the ancient Sith language.<ref name="JvS" /> [[Darth Andeddu]] lived early enough for his [[Holocron of Heresies|holocron]] to come into the possession of the fallen [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Freedon Nadd]].<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia">{{CSWECite|II|355|Nadd, Freedon}}</ref> He was known for experiments into eternal life, a possible link to the Rakatan term.<ref name="DOE">''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]''</ref>

But even if the Rakatan connection proves to have some validity, numerous other cultures make similar claims to the etymology of the title, so for the present, there is no definitive answer as to what the term "Darth" truly means.

===Usage===
====Ancient Sith====
Amongst the Sith Lords who held the title of Darth long before the time of Darth Sidious' successful conquest of the galaxy was [[Darth Andeddu]], a hoarder of Sith lore.<ref name="DOE" /> [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]], the last of the original [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lords of the Sith]] that ruled the old [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], held the title of Darth after ascending to the Sith throne just prior to waging the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]].<ref name="tegtw" />

====Revan and the Old Sith Wars====
[[File:RevanDLotS.jpg|thumb|right|100px|Darth Revan]]
As part of the [[Old Sith Wars]], the Jedi [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and [[Darth Malak|Malak]] betrayed the Republic after fighting in the Mandalorian Wars against the will of the Jedi Order, and the two descended to the dark side, styled themselves as Sith Lords, and took up the mantle of Darth. Malak betrayed Revan, his [[Sith Master/Legends|master]], and took an [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] of his own, dubbed [[Darth Bandon]].<ref name="KOTOR" /> After the fall of Darth Revan and Malak, the strongest remnants of their empire gathered to form the elusive [[Sith Triumvirate]], and the triumvirs each took up a Sith title containing the prefix Darth. The Lord of Betrayal styled herself as [[Kreia|Darth Traya]], whilst her apprentices, consumed by darkness, took up the names [[Darth Nihilus]] and [[Darth Sion]]. Traya was cast out by her pupils and came to be Kreia, the teacher of [[Meetra Surik]], who led the [[Lost Jedi]] during Sion and Nihilus' [[First Jedi Purge|Jedi purge]]. Surik wiped out the Sith Triumvirate, ridding the galaxy of the remnants of [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire]].<ref name="KOTOR 2" />

====Vitiate's reconstituted Empire====
[[File:DarthMalgus-Deceived.png|thumb|right|Also holding the title of Darth, Malgus served the Sith Emperor, Darth Vitiate]]
However, the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] that Lord [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] established when he came to power during the [[Post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion]] continued to grow outside of the Republic's borders. Vitiate took up the mantle of [[Sith Emperor/Legends|Sith Emperor]]<ref name="Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref> and Darth<ref name="FaDRulebook">[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]]</ref><ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> and allowed high-ranking Sith Lords of his reconstituted Empire to take up the title of Darth. Amongst the numerous Darths of Vitiate's reconstituted Empire were members of the [[Dark Council]], such as [[Darth Vengean|Vengean]] and [[Darth Vowrawn]], as well as enforcers of the Emperor's will on the battlefield such as [[Darth Malgus]].<ref name="SWTOR" />

====The New Sith Wars and the Brotherhood of Darkness====
{{Quote|Someone here once told me that the Darth title was no longer used because it promoted rivalry among the Sith. It gave the Jedi an easy target. It was easier just to abandon the custom. To have all the Sith Masters use the same title of Dark Lord. But I know the truth, Qordis. I know why none of you claim that name for yourself. Fear. You're cowards. None of the Brotherhood is worthy of the Darth title. Least of all you.|Darth Bane|<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction" />}}
The founding Sith Lord of the [[New Sith]], Darth Ruin, also used the title Darth, though there were few later Sith bearing the title until the rise of [[Darth Rivan]] and [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]].<ref name="JvS" /> During the [[Light and Darkness War]], [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Skere Kaan|Kaan]] discouraged the usage of the term within the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]], claiming that it promoted rivalry among the Sith. With the Sith of late suffering from constant infighting, Darth Bane believed that the concept of multiple Sith Lords diluted Sith power, and thought that the reason for prohibiting the use of the Darth title as merely the result of their fear of usurpation. Bane thus revived the use of the title for himself during the last days of the Brotherhood.<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction" />

===The Rule of Two===
[[File:SidSaber-ROTS.png|thumb|right|180px|Darth Sidious, who conquered the galaxy by becoming a duly elected [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Chancellor]] and successfully enacting the [[Grand Plan/Legends|Grand Plan]] of the Sith Lords.]]
Darth Bane, as the only survivor of the Sith Order after the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]],<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction" /> was largely able to reshape the Sith in his own image, instituting such reforms as the Sith of his lineage adopted the Darth title as he did,<ref name="ROT">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref> generally coupling it with a new Sith name (e.g. [[Darth Cognus|Cognus]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Sidious]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Vader]]), which was chosen for the apprentice by the master at the time the apprentice swore allegiance to the Sith.<ref name="DOE" /><ref name="DPN" /><ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Not all usages of the term "Darth" during this time, however, preceded a Sith name, as [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]] and [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] had the title of "Darth" preceding their birth names.<ref name="ROT" /><ref name="DPN" />

====The One Sith====
By the time of the [[One Sith]], the "Darth" title was reserved only for those who proved their power and their unquestioning loyalty to [[Darth Krayt]]. Others, such as [[Vul Isen]], were not entitled to the Darth title despite their expertise in the dark side of the Force, and weren't regarded as "real" Sith by some of the Darths.<ref name="Legacy 33" />

==Behind the scenes==
The title "Darth" first appeared in [[George Lucas]]' [[1977]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], as part of the name Darth Vader.<ref name="ANH" /> According to ''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'', Lucas intended the name "Darth Vader" to suggest "dark father."<ref name="BtM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref>

Darth is often thought to be a combination of letters from the title '''''Dar'''k Lord of the Si'''th''''', a theory which is alluded to in [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]. ''Darth'' may also be a portmanteau of ''dark'' and ''death''. Author and ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' lead writer [[Drew Karpyshyn]] hinted at a booksigning in Huntington Beach, California, that he likes to think the Darth title was around before the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]].

Prior to the release of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']], the only known Sith Lord to bear the title Darth was Darth Vader. When Darth Sidious (retroactively becoming the Sith name of Palpatine) and Darth Maul were revealed in ''The Phantom Menace'', the title took on its distinct association with the Sith, and it has appeared throughout all eras of the ''Star Wars'' saga. As a result of the popularity of ''Star Wars'', the term "Darth" has entered the popular lexicon as a term for evil. Most references are still associated with the ''Star Wars'' universe.

In [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] addresses [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] simply as ''Darth'', which is the only instance in the films where the word is used isolated. It is possible that at this point in the development of the saga "Darth" was intended to be the character's name, not a title; in-universe, possibly Obi-Wan was deliberately emphasizing the title as a way of taunting Vader and driving home what he had become.
